summary: The prepared main checkout still hardcoded sigmoid in Spark2_5Attention despite the gate_attn_act_mode configuration supported by the reference. The fix preserves the sigmoid default, dispatches sigmoid or silu in float32, and raises ValueError for unsupported modes. An existing open upstream candidate, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37727, was inspected before implementing the mirror delivery.

tests.what_was_measured: Regression collection failed because the checked-out implementation had no config-aware _apply_gate_activation helper; raw output: reports/j-ca26f1f6f593/raw/pytest-before.txt

Config default/propagation, exact float32 sigmoid and silu results over negative, zero, ordinary, and large inputs, dtype behavior, and rejection of an unsupported mode; raw output: reports/j-ca26f1f6f593/raw/pytest-after.txt

On gfx950, both activation modes matched independent formulas; sigmoid max_abs_diff=0, silu max_abs_diff=9.53674316e-07, while the pre-fix hardcoded sigmoid differed from the silu reference by 19; raw output: reports/j-ca26f1f6f593/raw/gpu-numerical.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 / HIP 7.2.26015; reports/j-ca26f1f6f593/raw/gpu-numerical.txt

remaining_limitations: No Spark-X2.5 weights were available, so no full-model or semantic-accuracy reproduction was performed. The GPU fixture validates only the corrected activation selection numerically, not accumulated model outputs or serving behavior. Released Spark-X2.5 checkpoints use sigmoid and therefore were not numerically affected by the original latent mismatch. No native code changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
